rationale: Retrieval supplied bound-style and sensitivity-analysis language, but the final downgrade is broadly the same packet-grounded move already achieved in v1.
Retrieval on Karlan-Zinman style designs and anticipated contract terms directly supports abandoning the selection-versus-incentive decomposition after the perturbation.
Retrieval materially strengthens the rejection of observational causal salvage by citing evidence on large nonexperimental advertising-measurement error.
Retrieval helps kill the remaining v1 failure mode by explicitly rejecting exposure-level IV/LATE recovery and centering the assignment-level ITT instead.
Retrieval on within-store interference bias and contaminated untreated comparisons directly supports dropping the residual within-store DiD/salience salvage that survived in v1.

The final downgrade to a menu-announcement bundle ITT follows the packet logic cleanly; retrieval adds support but does not appear to change the qualitative design choice relative to a strong critic-only run.
Retrieval sharpens the measurement argument by reinforcing the distinction between reporting effects and true corruption effects, supporting a reporting-only ITT.
The retrieved self-report measurement literature is central to the memo's downgrade from actual-behavior claims to self-reported ITT plus sensitivity analysis.
Retrieval supports the descriptive fallback, but v1 had already made the key downgrade; the extra search does not visibly change the final estimand choice.

The final memo still lands on the correct bundle-only estimand, but retrieval incurred a semantic-scholar rate-limit event and one off-topic deepxiv result, so the search layer added noise rather than a clearly better design move.
